note: Round-3 candidate list for Experiment A2 (Arm 1, PUBLISHED-INT8), assembled 2026-09-23 by the A2 top-up agent under results/paper/a2_design_registered.md sections 1-2. It ADDS to results/expA/candidates.json (17) and results/expA2/candidates_round2.json (19); it replaces neither. Reason for the round: the admitted pool stood at 13, below the registered minimum of 18 (section 4). NO A2 CHECKER OUTPUT EXISTED WHEN THIS FILE WAS WRITTEN: results/expA2 held only pool.json, manifest.json, candidates_round2.json and stage_records/, with no predictions.json, no selftest.json and no results/paper/a2_predictions_frozen.md - so D13's rule that no candidate may be added after the first A2 checker output is not breached, and nothing here was chosen with a flag in hand.
collector: A2 top-up agent (round 3 of the one registered fetch round, 2.1)
verification_policy: Every candidate in this list was PRE-SCREENED FROM THE FILE before being written down: the collector fetched each URL once, anonymously, into a scratch directory, read the graph with a_pool.check_static(exp='A2') - the same code the admission stage runs - recorded the sha256, byte count, opset, node count, Q/DQ counts and static/dynamic activation-site counts, and deleted the file. No candidate is listed on the strength of its name, its model card or a quantize_config.json: 12 of the 21 files pre-screened were rejected on the graph alone, and they are listed under known_rejections_no_download. The pipeline fetches each URL again and ITS sha256, byte count and rule verdicts are the record; where the two disagree the pipeline governs. Licence states in this file are the collector's reading and are informational only - stage_licence_a2 re-derives every state from the publisher's hub metadata before the fetch (VA15).

known_rejections_no_download.name: onnxmodelzoo/* (densenet-12-int8, googlenet-12-int8, mnist-12-int8, caffenet-12-int8, fcn-resnet50-12-int8, ResNet101-DUC-12-int8, arcfaceresnet100-11-int8, zfnet512-12-int8, vgg16-12-int8 and the -qdq siblings)
known_rejections_no_download.rule: NOT PUT UP, by the collector's decision, recorded here so a reader can overturn it. These repositories are a Hugging Face mirror of the ONNX Model Zoo: the files are the same Intel Neural Compressor artefacts as github.com/onnx/models, and several are byte-identical to files already in this pool (onnxmodelzoo/squeezenet1.0-12-int8 is 1,293,388 B, the size of the admitted b15; efficientnet-lite4-11-qdq, emotion-ferplus-12-int8 and version-RFB-320-int8 match a04, a05 and a06 byte for byte). Admitting them under the publisher name 'onnxmodelzoo' would take the ONNX Model Zoo past A9a's per-publisher cap of 6, which onnx/models has already reached, and would add nothing to A11's export-tooling census. Independently, results/expA2/candidates_round2.json already records onnxmodelzoo/googlenet-12-qdq as L1 INDETERMINATE (metadata says apache-2.0 while the card body carries SPDX BSD-3-Clause and a dead LICENSE link), and stage_licence_a2 reads only the metadata, so these rows would be recorded DECLARED in contradiction of that finding.

known_rejections_no_download.rule: L1 INDETERMINATE -> L2 / abort 6'. Each of these repositories carries a LICENSE file in its root and states no licence identifier in the hub metadata, which is exactly L1's 'no identifier in the metadata but a licence file in the root: the terms cannot be resolved to an identifier'. Only opencv/facial_expression_recognition has no licence file in its root, which is why c04 is the single OpenCV candidate. Several of these ship a '_int8.onnx' from the zoo's own static quantization tooling and are well inside A7, so this is a licence-state rejection and not a technical one.

collector_notes: SEARCH ACTUALLY PERFORMED, so a reader can see what was not searched: the Hugging Face model API by author for CoreEpoch, Thefalley, Arm, ketiswp, onnx, amd, AMD-PAVS-AI, opencv, onnxmodelzoo, qualcomm, FasterAI-Labs, mohitsha, Evintkoo, haidangung, fxmarty and deepghs; by name substring for int8, quantized, qdq, u8s8, ptq, w8a8, static-int8, int8-qop, int8-imagenet, kenosis, vit-int8, swin-int8, deit-int8, yolo11, yolov8, rtmdet, nanodet, mobileone, fastvit, levit and poolformer, with and without the onnx tag; by pipeline tag over image-classification, object-detection, image-segmentation, keypoint-detection, depth-estimation and image-feature-extraction; and the hub's full-text search for quantize_static, vai_q_onnx and QuantFormat.QDQ. GitHub releases and vendor model zoos outside Hugging Face were NOT put up, for a mechanical reason: stage_licence_a2 can read a licence state only from the Hugging Face model API or from an onnx/models README, so any other host resolves to INDETERMINATE and is dropped by L2 before it is fetched. The OpenCV Zoo on GitHub is the largest source this excludes.

WHY SO FEW TRANSFORMERS: of everything this search reached, exactly four statically quantized vision-transformer or hybrid files under 60 MB with fixed C,H,W exist on the hub - CoreEpoch's three (already admitted as b01-b03) and haidangung's Depth-Anything-V2-Small (c08) - plus one behind a gate (c10). Every other quantized transformer export the search returned was transformers.js/quantize_dynamic output (dynamic activations), gated, over 60 MB, or shape-free. That is a fact about what is published, and it is the same fact A2 section 4 predicted would bind.

THE AMD QUESTION, ANSWERED FROM THE REPOSITORIES: the six AMD candidates rejected at A3 in round 2 (b07-b12) cannot be rescued by choosing a different file, because each of those six repositories publishes exactly one INT8 ONNX file - amd/squeezenet additionally has SqueezeNet_fp32.onnx, which fails A3 by construction, and no other file in any of the six is an .onnx. What is NOT true is that the rejection is a property of AMD's toolchain: three other AMD repositories (efficientnet-es, mobilenet_v2_1.0_224, sesr) publish genuine static QDQ graphs with 328, 342 and 66 8-bit Q/DQ nodes, and they are c01-c03 here. The six rejected files carry no quantization operators of any kind in the published graph while their siblings from the same publisher do.

PAIR-REPLICATE HYGIENE: ketiswp/onnx-model-zoo-MobileNetV2 and ketiswp/onnx-model-zoo-ShuffleNetV2 were pre-screened, both are static (66 and 76 static activation sites) and both would pass A1-A5 - but each is a second quantization variant of a base checkpoint already admitted (a02 mobilenetv2-12-qdq, a01 shufflenet-v2-12-qdq), and base_checkpoint_key cannot see that across two publishers, so A10 would score them as two independent matrix rows instead of one row and one PAIR-REPLICATE. They were dropped for that reason alone, and for no other. c09 is the ketiswp candidate whose base checkpoint (STM32AI MobileNetV2 0.5) is genuinely absent from the pool.
